payload.claim: Criterion 1's second wrong_versions entry ("A stub added under the wrong dotted path, such as saffron.gates.suite.CellTree.spec_ids, so worktree.spec_ids itself still reaches runtime.exec_ and the real argv still appears") is false and not caught by the criterion's own named witness. I built this exact mutant against the snapshot with the prescribed fix otherwise in place, and the new witness test (test_the_generic_stub_answers_spec_ids_without_a_real_grep_call) passed under it instead of failing: patching the class attribute CellTree.spec_ids fully replaces the bound method tree.spec_ids() calls, so worktree.spec_ids (and runtime.exec_) is never reached and no real argv appears in cell.execs — the opposite of what the entry claims. The mutant is only caught, incidentally, by the unrelated witness of criterion 2 (test_the_lens_gate_cell_holds_no_credential_and_is_gone_before_any_lens_runs). I confirmed via saffron/phases/review.py::run_wrong_versions and saffron/cell/session.py::_apply_criterion_probes that wrong_versions entries are not illustrative prose: the repo's own review phase turns each into a real source edit and applies it, then asks that criterion's own named witness — exactly the failure mode documented in docs/evidence/2026-11-13-spec-loop-skill-feedback-run-68.md ("a wrong_versions entry neither witness could kill"). Building this criterion exactly as written will very plausibly reproduce that failure during review, after a cell has already spent money. wrong_versions 1 and 3 of this same criterion were verified to be correctly caught by the named witness.
